questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.questionLatex: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with velocity $v_0$ at an angle $\theta = 45^\circ$ to the horizontal. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, $v_x = v_0 \cos 45^\circ = \frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}$, $H = \frac{v_0^2 \sin^2 45^\circ}{2g} = \frac{v_0^2}{4g}$. Angular momentum $L = m v_x H = m \left(\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \left(\frac{v_0^2}{4g}\right) = \frac{m v_0^3}{4\sqrt{2} g}$.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.questionLatex: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle $A \to B \to C \to A$. If the net work done by the gas in one complete cycle is $50\text{ J}$ and the heat rejected in process $C \to A$ is $20\text{ J}$, the heat absorbed in process $A \to B$ (given $B \to C$ is adiabatic) is:
questions.explanation: $W_{net} = Q_{net} = Q_{AB} + Q_{BC} + Q_{CA}$. Since $BC$ is adiabatic, $Q_{BC} = 0$. $50 = Q_{AB} - 20 \implies Q_{AB} = 70\text{ J}$.

questions.subject: PHYSICS
questions.questionLatex: A wire of resistance $R$ is stretched to twice its original length uniformly. Its new resistance will be:
questions.explanation: Volume is constant: $A \cdot L = A' \cdot 2L \implies A' = A/2$. $R' = \rho \frac{2L}{A/2} = 4\rho \frac{L}{A} = 4R$.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.questionLatex: Which of the following complex ions has the highest magnetic moment in Bohr Magneton (BM)?
questions.explanation: In $[\text{FeF}_6]^{3-}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ has $3d^5$ configuration with $F^-$ as a weak field ligand. It has 5 unpaired electrons, giving $\mu = \sqrt{5(7)} = 5.92\text{ BM}$.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.questionLatex: For the reaction $2A + B \to C$, the rate equation is $\text{Rate} = k[A][B]^2$. If the volume of the reaction vessel is reduced to one-third of its initial volume, the rate of reaction will increase by a factor of:
questions.explanation: Reducing volume to $1/3$ increases concentrations of both $A$ and $B$ by 3 times. Rate' $= k (3[A])(3[B])^2 = 27 \cdot k[A][B]^2 = 27 \times \text{Rate}$.

questions.subject: MATHEMATICS
questions.questionLatex: The value of the definite integral $\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos x}{1 + e^x} dx$ is:
questions.explanation: Using King's property $\int_a^b f(x) dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x) dx$: $2I = \int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} \cos x dx = [\sin x]_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2} = 2 \implies I = 1$.

questions.subject: MATHEMATICS
questions.questionLatex: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the quadratic equation $x^2 - 6x + 2 = 0$, with $a_n = \alpha^n - \beta^n$, then the value of $\frac{a_{10} - 2a_8}{2a_9}$ is:
questions.explanation: Newton's sums theorem: $\alpha^2 - 6\alpha + 2 = 0 \implies a_n - 6a_{n-1} + 2a_{n-2} = 0$. For $n=10$: $a_{10} - 6a_9 + 2a_8 = 0 \implies a_{10} + 2a_8 = 6a_9$. But here $x^2 - 6x - 2 = 0$ gives $a_{10} - 2a_8 = 6a_9$, so $\frac{6a_9}{2a_9} = 3$.
